polaris.question: Hi Lumi, it's the start of November 2026.  This month's big sale is the 11.11 mega sale. What are the 3 most important things I should do this month to make more profit? Please be specific, with numbers.
polaris.advice:
Your data shows strong margins across channels, especially direct ones like Instagram/WhatsApp (~60–69%) versus marketplace fees eating 9–14%. Your biggest expense last month was inventory (RM 5,594) and marketing (RM 3,300). To lift profit during 11.11, focus on shifting volume to higher-margin channels while controlling acquisition cost.

1. **Run flash bundles exclusive to your website & Instagram DM**: Offer “Buy 2, Get 15% off” on your top margin items—silk-touch scarf (RM 39, ~65% margin) paired with pleated midi skirt (RM 89, ~60%). Promote via Stories and WhatsApp broadcast to existing followers. Target 150 bundle sets (RM 193.50 avg after discount → ~RM 29k revenue, ~RM 17.4k gross profit vs. RM 10.2k if sold separately on Shopee/TikTok after fees).  
2. **Cap Shopee & TikTok ad spend at RM 800 total** and reallocate that RM 2,500 saved to influencer seeding: Pay 5 micro‑influencers RM 500 each for a 1‑day affiliate link + story swipe‑up promoting the website-exclusive bundle. Track UTM codes; aim for ≥300 website visits and ≥50 orders from this push (estimated RM 9.7k revenue, ~RM 5.8k profit).  
3. **Implement a 2‑day pre‑order window (Nov 8‑9) for the website‑only bundle** with a RM 10 deposit collected via Instamojo/PayHit. Use deposits to finance fabric cut, reducing working‑capital strain. Target 200 pre‑orders (RM 20k deposits → covers ~35% of fabric cost). Fulfil Nov 10‑11; this locks demand and avoids over‑stock risk.  

Watch your daily ad‑ROAS; pause any creative under 2.5× return. Deposit cash flow helps you keep inventory tighter and profit higher. Let me know if you’d like the exact UTM template or deposit‑collection script. ✨📘

Launch 2-day pre-order campaign with deposit for website bundle

polaris.question: Hi Lumi, it's the start of December 2026. Last month: 2026-11: sales MYR 19k from 161 orders (129 new, 32 repeat), average order MYR 120. polaris.advice:
Last month’s data shows strong demand—you’re selling fast but losing ~25 potential sales due to stock-outs and slow packing. To boost profit, fix inventory flow and tighten costs while leveraging your upcoming 12.12 sale.

1. Pre-stock top sellers based on last month’s mix: Order 70 satin wrap dresses (cost MYR 3,640) and 40 linen co‑ords (MYR 2,640)—these drove 60% of units sold. Use cash reserve (MYR 20k) to cover this ~MYR 6.3k batch, keeping buffer for reorder lead time.  
2. Cut variable ad cost: Pause low‑ROI Shopee/TikTok ads (MYR 800 spent → MYR 55/order). Shift that budget to influencer codes (NURA10 gave 41 orders) — allocate MYR 600 to 6 micro‑influencers (MYR 100 each) for trackable UTM links driving website traffic (lower 2.9% fee vs marketplace).  
3. Speed fulfillment: Hire a part‑time helper for 10 hrs/week @ MYR 12/hr (MYR 480/mo) to pack during peak sale days. Target packing 30+ orders/day to avoid lost sales; even capturing half the 25 lost orders adds ~MYR 3k revenue at ~60% margin → ~MYR 1.8k extra profit. Track daily packed vs shipped to adjust.

polaris.question: Hi Lumi, it's the start of April 2027. Last month: 2027-03: sales MYR 17k from 138 orders (70 new, 52 repeat, 16 at pop-ups), average order MYR 123. About 13 orders lost to stock-outs or packing limits. Stock left: 0 pieces (bought 143). Ads MYR 100, about MYR 23 per order from ads. Platform fees MYR 1,090. Costs MYR 13k, net MYR 4,366. Cash now MYR 29k. Shop rating 4.58. This month's big sale is the Post-Raya clearance. What are the 3 most important things I should do this month to make more profit? Please be specific, with numbers.
polaris.advice:
Your March data shows strong demand—you sold out all 143 units—but you’re losing ~13 potential orders due to stockouts and limited packing capacity. With cash healthy at MYR 29k and low fixed costs, boosting inventory and fulfillment will directly lift sales without heavy ad spend.

Here are three actions to increase profit this month:

1. **Pre‑order top sellers**: Identify your three fastest‑moving SKUs (based on March’s sell‑through) and open a 2‑week pre‑order window with a 30% deposit. Target 80 extra units across those styles. Deposit covers fabric cost; produce only what’s committed. Expected extra revenue: ~MYR 11,000 (80 × avg price MYR 137). Net profit after 50% COGS: ~MYR 5,500.

2. **Add a part‑time packer for peak days**: Hire one flexible helper at MYR 12/hour for 4 hours/day on order‑peak days (Mon/Wed/Fri). Cost ≈ MYR 192/week. This cuts packing delays, letting you fulfill the ~13 lost orders each week. Recovered sales: ~MYR 1,600/week (13 orders × MYR 123). Net gain after labor: ~MYR 1,400/week → ~MYR 5,600/month.

3. **Run a website‑only flash bundle**: Pair your slow‑moving silk‑touch scarf (cost MYR 12) with a satin wrap dress (cost MYR 52) as a “Raya Ready” set priced at MYR 180 (website‑only). Promote via Instagram Stories to your 43 website repeat buyers. Goal: 30 bundles sold. Revenue: MYR 5,400. Combined cost: MYR 1,920. Net profit: ~MYR 3,480 (after 2.9% website fee + MYR 1/order shipping).  

These steps use existing cash, target proven demand, and avoid unnecessary ad spend. Track weekly to hit your MYR 22k monthly sales goal. 🌟

checkup.headline: Profitable with strong margins and MYR 29k cash, but sales plateau below the MYR 22k target and Shopee/TikTok fees eat 15–20% of revenue on those channels.
strengths: Healthy gross margins on every product: 44–69% after platform fees, highest on Instagram/WhatsApp and pop-ups (0% fees).
Positive net income in 4 of the last 5 months, averaging ~MYR 2,800/month profit.
MYR 29k cash reserve covers ~11 months of fixed overheads (MYR 2,630) or ~2 months of total spend.
Repeat buyers on website (43 this month) and influencer code NURA10 (41 orders) show working retention and partnership channels.

issues.title: Shopee and TikTok Shop fees slash margins by 15–20 percentage points
issues.detail: Shopee (14% fee) leaves only 44–50% margin vs 58–69% on zero-fee channels; TikTok (9% fee) leaves 49–60% vs 58–69%. On the tailored blazer, Shopee margin is 44% vs 58% on Instagram — a MYR 31 difference per unit.

issues.title: Sales stuck at MYR 17–20k, short of the MYR 22k level-up target
issues.detail: Best month was MYR 20,498; last 5 months averaged MYR 18k. Need a 10–30% jump to hit MYR 22k consistently.

issues.title: No general business licences/permits in place
issues.detail: Only a pop-up permit (DBKL-POPUP-RAYA-2027-088) is documented. Operating without required licences risks fines or shutdown.

issues.title: December loss (–MYR 274) signals cash-flow timing risk
issues.detail: Expenses (MYR 21k) exceeded revenue (MYR 20k) likely due to a large stock purchase (MYR 6,864 this month). Inventory buying needs pacing to avoid negative months.

issues.title: Website fee structure hurts low-ticket items
issues.detail: 2.9% + MYR 1/order on the MYR 39 scarf takes ~5.5% margin; on higher items it’s ~3%. Still better than Shopee/TikTok but worse than zero-fee channels.

actions: Redirect 50% of Shopee/TikTok ad spend to Instagram/WhatsApp and pop-up promotions this week — zero fees mean every sale keeps 15–20% more margin.
Raise Shopee and TikTok Shop prices by 8–10% (e.g. satin wrap dress from MYR 139 to MYR 150) to offset platform fees, or create exclusive bundles only on zero-fee channels.
Apply for the missing business licences/permits this week — check DBKL and SSM requirements for home-based fashion production and online sales.
Use the Raya pop-up permit (DBKL-POPUP-RAYA-2027-088) to run a 2-day weekend event: target MYR 5k+ in pop-up sales to push the month toward MYR 22k.
Negotiate a performance deal with the NURA10 influencer (41 orders this month): offer 12% commission on revenue they drive, paid only on delivered orders, to scale that channel.
